chronic intermittent hypoxia up-regulates NADPH oxidases and causes a modest increase in oxidative stress in rat sternohoid muscle.
chronic intermittent hypoxia causes an increase in NADPH oxidases in rat sternohoyoid muscle with attendant modest oxidative and antioxidant stress.
chronic intermittent hypoxia exposure upregulates NADPH oxidases in sternohyoids and this results in a small increase in reactive oxygen species and a decrease in force and power.

understanding the molecular basis of CIH-induced upper-airway muscle dysfunction.
the role of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the pathophysiology of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and its complications.
